title: Which option? Scoring architecture choices
objective: Learners compare three or four architecture options scored on five criteria, apply a weighting profile, and see that the weighted score (the number a steering committee asks for) is decided by the weights, not by the options; and they see three honest ways to show it: a radar, parallel coordinates, and bullet graphs against a target.

recommended.why: A radar per option is the picture committees expect; Chart.js draws it from configuration and the host clock can reveal one axis at a time.

alternative.why: The radar shows shape; parallel coordinates show every option as a line across the criteria and make the trade-offs legible with four options. Which one would you put in the decision paper?

assumptions: Options, scores and weighting profiles are illustrative for a fictional integration decision; no vendor or product is being rated
Every criterion is scored 1 to 10 with higher better; operational burden is scored as its inverse so that 10 means little burden
The weighted score is the weighted mean of the criteria scored out of 100; the four profiles are balanced, cost first, compliance first and speed first
Bands: 70 and above is good, 50 to 69 acceptable, below 50 poor; the target is the minimum the chosen option must clear
Playback: four scenes over about 17 s (criteria, weights, verdict, so what)
checkDescription: Weighted scores recompute from the raw scores and the profile weights, the winner and runner-up are the top two scores with the stated margin, bands and target flags follow the score, raw scores do not change with the profile, and under the balanced profile the ranking equals the ranking by mean score.

learnerPrompts.predict: Switch to Cost first before you play. Which option wins now, and by how much?
learnerPrompts.explain: Include "keep it manual" and set Cost first. It now scores above the integration platform. Explain to the committee why the radar and the parallel coordinates would have stopped that number being taken seriously.
